rules.title: Annual Rent Increase Cap Tied to CPI, Max 4%
rules.requirement: Landlords may not raise rent for a housing space at lease expiration or termination of a periodic tenancy by more than the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index measured from 15 months prior to 3 months prior to the proposed increase, and in no case may the increase exceed 4%.
rules.key_value: CPI increase (15mo to 3mo prior), capped at 4%

coverage_conditions.notes: Applies to all multiple dwellings as defined in the ordinance (buildings with one or more apartments rented to tenants); exemptions apply to public housing, hotels/motels, commercial space, newly constructed multiple dwellings, vacant dwellings, and certain subsidized/Section 8 units.

rules.exemptions: Public housing; hotel/motel day-to-day rentals; commercial space; newly constructed multiple dwellings (per 19:2-18.1); vacant dwellings (per 19:2-18.2); units in Federal/State Rental Rehabilitation Programs receiving Section 8 subsidies (rent capped at HUD fair market rent during subsidy tenure); units under governmental agency rent-regulation contracts that preempt City regulation during the contract term.
rules.interaction: Allowable annual increase is denied if the dwelling is not in substantial compliance with codes or if the landlord has not met registration requirements under 19:2-9.8.
rules.quoted_span: no landlord may request or receive an increase greater than the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the CPI fifteen (15) months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase to the CPI three (3) months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase. In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed four (4%) percent.

rules.title: Tax Surcharge Passed Through to Tenants
rules.requirement: A landlord may seek an additional rent surcharge from tenants to cover increases in municipal property taxes, calculated proportionally based on each tenant's share of the total rent roll, subject to Board approval and 30 days' notice.
rules.key_value: surcharge = (annual tax increase / 12) / total monthly rent roll x tenant's monthly rent
rules.exemptions: Denied or deferred if outstanding code violations exist on the property until abated.
rules.interaction: Tenant also entitled to proportional tax decrease rebates and 75% of successful tax appeal reductions under 19:2-6.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord shall divide one-twelfth (1/12th) of the annual increase in the present property tax over the property tax of the previous year by the total monthly rent roll, and that product shall be multiplied by the monthly rent paid by each tenant to establish the amount of surcharge that each tenant shall be required to pay.

rules.title: Major New Improvement Surcharge
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge tenants an additional rent surcharge to recover the cost of a major new improvement, prorated by useful life and apportioned among benefiting tenants, with caps on scope and timing.
rules.key_value: No increase for improvements affecting more than 10 units unless total cost exceeds $2,000; no increase if completed more than 24 months before notice to Board
rules.exemptions: No increase permitted if dwelling is not in substantial compliance or landlord has not met registration requirements.
rules.quoted_span: No increase shall be permitted for major new improvement(s) affecting more than ten (10) rental units, unless the total cost thereof exceeds two thousand ($2,000.00) dollars.

rules.title: Hardship Rent Increase for Fair Rate of Return
rules.requirement: A landlord unable to earn a fair rate of return (5% on equity investment) may apply to the Rent Control Board for a hardship rent increase above the normal CPI cap, subject to Board hearing, inspection for code compliance, and documentation requirements.
rules.key_value: Fair rate of return = 5% on landlord's equity investment
rules.exemptions: Denied if dwelling not in substantial compliance; denied in whole or part if landlord purchased dwelling at excessive price or incurred expenses an efficient operator would not incur.
rules.interaction: No increase authorized more than once per 12-month period per rental unit; prior rent increases of any kind in past 12 months considered.
rules.quoted_span: a landlord may appeal to the Board for a hardship rent increase if the landlord is unable to meet its reasonable and necessary operating expenses and earn a fair rate of return on his investment
